chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hussein ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadhdha, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
Indeed, when a believer shakes hands with a believer, they depart from each other void of any sin.

key_terms.صَافَحَ: to shake hands or greet with a handshake

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of shaking hands between believers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to highlight the social dimension of spiritual purification, where the physical act of greeting (safah) serves as a mechanism for clearing interpersonal debts and grievances. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining communal harmony, suggesting that even minor social interactions can serve as expiation (kaffarah) for sins committed against one another, thereby preserving the purity of the believer's record.
